facts.statement: The genus Yangchuanosaurus was named after the discovery location of Yongchuan in China.
facts.quote: This theropod was named after the area in which was discovered, Yongchuan, in China.

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus lived in China during the Middle Jurassic to Late Jurassic periods, specifically from the Bathonian to Tithonian stages.
facts.quote: Yangchuanosaurus is an extinct genus of metriacanthosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived in China from the Middle Jurassic to Late Jurassic periods (Bathonian to Tithonian stages)

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus was the largest predator in its ecosystem, sharing the Upper Shaximiao Formation with sauropods like Mamenchisaurus and stegosaurs like Tuojiangosaurus.
facts.quote: Yangchuanosaurus hails from the Upper Shaximiao Formation and was the largest predator in a landscape that included the sauropods Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus, and the stegosaurs Chialingosaurus, Tuojiangosaurus, and Chungkingosaurus.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Yangchuanosaurus was discovered in June 1977 by a construction worker building the Shangyou Reservoir Dam.
facts.quote: It was discovered in June 1977 by a construction worker during the construction of the Shangyou Reservoir Dam.

facts.statement: Dong et al. named the species Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis in 1978 based on a complete skull and skeleton found near Yongchuan, Sichuan.
facts.quote: Dong et al. (1978) named Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis on the basis of Municipal Museum of Chongqing 00215, a complete skull and skeleton which was collected from the Shangshaximiao Formation, near Yongchuan, Yongchuan District, Sichuan.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Yangchuanosaurus dates to the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, approximately 161.2 to 157.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: It dates to the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic period, about 161.2 to 157.3 million years ago.

facts.statement: A 2012 phylogenetic study by Carrano, Benson, and Sampson concluded that the two named species of Yangchuanosaurus are actually the same species.
facts.quote: A detailed revision of tetanuran phylogeny by Carrano, Benson & Sampson (2012) revealed that both species are conspecific.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul suggested in 1988 that Yangchuanosaurus should be considered a synonym of Metriacanthosaurus, but this view was not supported by later research.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul (1988) regarded this genus as a synonym of Metriacanthosaurus, but this has not been supported.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis had a skull measuring 82 cm in length and a total body length estimated at 8 meters.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Y. shangyouensis had a skull 82 cm long, and its total body length was estimated at 8 m.

facts.statement: A larger specimen assigned to the species Y. magnus had a skull length of 1.11 meters.
facts.quote: Another specimen, assigned to the new species Y. magnus, was even larger, with a skull length of 1.11 m.

facts.statement: The larger species Y. magnus may have reached a length of up to 10.8 meters and weighed as much as 3.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: It may have been up to 10.8 m long, and weighed as much as 3.4 MT.

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus had a small dewclaw on the first digit of its foot, while the three outer toes bore weight and each possessed a large claw.
facts.quote: The first digit of its foot was a small dewclaw. The three outer toes were used to bear weight and each was equipped with a large claw.

facts.statement: A 2012 analysis identified Yangchuanosaurus as the most basal known metriacanthosaurid and the only one outside the Metriacanthosaurinae subfamily.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis by Carrano et al. (2012) found Yangchuanosaurus to be the basalmost known metriacanthosaurid and the only non-metriacanthosaurine metriacanthosaurid.

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus lived in Asia from the Middle to Late Jurassic, approximately 170 to 157 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Oxfordian stages.
facts.quote: Yangchuanosaurus ("lagarto de Yang-chuan") es un género con dos especies conocidas de dinosaurios terópodos metriacantosáuridos, que vivieron de mediados a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 170 a 157 millones de años, desde el Bathoniense al Oxfordiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus belongs to the family Metriacanthosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Metriacanthosauridae

facts.statement: The genus Yangchuanosaurus was described by Dong et al. in 1978.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Dong et al., 1978

facts.statement: The classification of Y.? hepingensis is debated, with some paleontologists questioning its identity within Sinraptor while others, like Rauhut and colleagues, place it within Yangchuanosaurus based on phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: However, the identity of this species within Sinraptor is questioned by other paleontologists, and Rauhut and colleagues included this species within Yangchuanosaurus based on their phylogenetic analysis in 2019 and 2024 respectively.

facts.statement: It is debated whether CV 00214 and Szechuanosaurus zigongensis are the same species, as Carrano et al. noted they lack shared unique traits and come from different geological formations.
facts.quote: Carrano et al. (2012) suggested that CV 00214 and "S." zigongensis cannot be conspecific, as there are no autapomorphies shared between them, and the latter derives from the underlying Xiashaximiao Formation.

facts.statement: The assignment of Szechuanosaurus zigongensis to Yangchuanosaurus is considered questionable by Rauhut and colleagues despite its close relationship to Y. shangyouensis.
facts.quote: Furthermore, Szechuanosaurus zigongensis was found to be closely related to Y. shangyouensis and therefore was designated as a new species of Yangchuanosaurus, though this has been considered questionable by Rauhut and colleagues.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Y. shangyouensis had a skull 82 centimeters long and an estimated total body length of 8 meters.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo de Y. shangyouensis tenía un cráneo de 82 centímetros de largo y la longitud total de su cuerpo se estimó en 8 metros.

facts.statement: Another specimen, originally assigned to the new species Y. magnus, had a skull length of 1.11 meters.
facts.quote: Otro espécimen, originalmente asignado a la nueva especie, Y. magnus, era aún más grande, con una longitud de cráneo de 1,11 metros.

facts.statement: The animal may have reached a length of up to 10.8 meters and weighed up to 3.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Puede haber tenido hasta 10,8 metros de largo y pesar hasta 3,4 toneladas métricas.

facts.statement: It had a bony crest on its nose and multiple horns and crests, similar to Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: Había una cresta ósea en su nariz y múltiples cuernos y crestas, similar a Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: It possessed a long tail that reached half the total body length.
facts.quote: Poseían una larga cola que alcanzaba la mitad de la longitud total del cuerpo.

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus was a large and powerful carnivore.
facts.quote: Yangchuanosaurus era un carnívoro grande y poderoso.

facts.statement: It walked on two large, muscular legs, had short arms, a short and strong neck, a large head with powerful jaws, and large serrated teeth.
facts.quote: Caminaba sobre dos piernas grandes y musculosas, tenía brazos cortos, un cuello corto y fuerte, una cabeza grande con mandíbulas poderosas y dientes grandes y aserrados.

facts.statement: It was a fast runner that used three-toed feet and hands with sharp, curved claws to grab prey like sauropods Mamenchisaurus and Omeisaurus.
facts.quote: Era un rápido corredor, sus patas y manos tenían tres dedos con garras afiladas y curvas con las que se prendía a su presa como saurópodos Mamenchisaurus y Omeisaurus.

facts.statement: It was discovered in June 1977 by a construction worker during the construction of the Shangyou reservoir dam.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en junio de 1977 por un trabajador de la construcción durante la construcción de la presa del embalse de Shangyou.

facts.statement: It lived during the Oxfordian stage of the Late Jurassic, between 161.2 and 157.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Data de la etapa oxfordiense del período Jurásico tardío, hace entre 161,2 y 157,3 millones de años.

facts.statement: Dong et al. named Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis in 1978 based on CV 00215, a complete skull and skeleton collected from the Shangshaximiao Formation near Yongchuan, Sichuan.
facts.quote: Dong et al. en 1978 nombrarón a Yangchuanosaurus shangyouensis sobre la base de CV 00215, un cráneo y un esqueleto completos que se recolectaron de la Formación Shangshaximiao, cerca de Yongchuan, distrito de Yongchuan, Sichuan.

facts.statement: A second species from the same locality, Y. magnus, was named by Dong et al. in 1983 based on CV 00216, another complete skull and skeleton.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie de la misma localidad, Y. magnus, fue nombrada por Dong et al. en 1983 sobre la base de CV 00216, otro cráneo y esqueleto completos.

facts.statement: A detailed phylogenetic review by Carrano, Benson, and Sampson in 2012 revealed that both species are conspecific.
facts.quote: Una revisión detallada de la filogenia del tetanuro realizada por Carrano, Benson y Sampson en 2012 reveló que ambas especies son conespecíficas.

facts.statement: Yangchuanosaurus zigongensis is known from four specimens, including holotype ZDM 9011 (partial postcranial skeleton), ZDM 9012 (left maxilla), ZDM 9013 (two teeth), and ZDM 9014 (right hind limb).
facts.quote: Yangchuanosaurus zigongensis se conoce a partir de cuatro especímenes, incluido su holotipo ZDM 9011, un esqueleto poscraneal parcial, ZDM 9012, un maxilar izquierdo, ZDM 9013, dos dientes y ZDM 9014, un miembro posterior derecho.

facts.statement: It was first described by Gao in 1993, with all specimens collected from the Middle Jurassic Xiashaximiao Formation at the Dashanpu Dinosaur Quarry in Zigong, Sichuan.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por primera vez por Gao en 1993, y todos los especímenes fueron recolectados de la Formación Xiashaximiao del Jurásico Medio en la Cantera de Dinosaurios Dashanpu de Zigong, Sichuan.

facts.statement: An informal third species, Yangchuanosaurus "longqiaoensis", was briefly mentioned in a fauna list from the Penglaizhen Formation; initially thought to be Late Jurassic, it is likely Early Cretaceous (Berriasian to Valanginian) according to Li, Zhang, and Cai in 1999.
facts.quote: Una tercera especie informal, Yangchuanosaurus "longqiaoensis", fue mencionada brevemente en una lista de fauna de la Formación Penglaizhen, inicialmente se creía que databa del Jurásico tardío, pero probablemente era del Cretácico temprano, Berriasiense al Valanginiense en edad por Li, Zhang y Cai en 1999.

facts.statement: A phylogenetic analysis by Carrano et al. in 2012 found that Yangchuanosaurus is the most basal known metriacanthosaurid and the only non-metriacantosaurine metriacanthosaurid.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético de Carrano et al. en 2012 encontraron que Yangchuanosaurus es el metriacantosáurido conocido más basal y el único metriacantosáurido no metriacantosaurino.

facts.statement: The genus time range spans from the Bajocian to the Aptian (170.9 to 113.2 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Bajocian to Aptian (170.9 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Yangchuanosaurus was a large, powerful meat-eater. It walked on two large, muscular legs, had short arms, a strong, short neck, a big head with powerful jaws, and large, serrated teeth.
